title: Theory of Magnetic Excitations in the Heavy-Fermion Spin-Triplet Superconductor UTe$_2$
authors: Koki Shimura, Shuntaro Sumita, Yusuke Kato
abstract: We study the dynamical spin response of UTe$_2$ by using a mixed-dimensional periodic Anderson model. Within the BCS-RPA formalism, we examine how the $f$-orbital character of the quasiparticles affects magnetic excitations in both the normal and superconducting (SC) states. In the normal state, finite mixing between localized $f$ electrons and conduction electrons produces a hybridization gap and enhances the spin response at $\mathbf{Q}_{\mathrm{Y}} = (0,π,0)$, indicating that the magnetic excitation originates from particle--hole scattering across the hybridization gap. In the SC state, we compare four odd-parity irreducible representations, $A_u$, $B_{1u}$, $B_{2u}$, and $B_{3u}$, for the spin-triplet order parameter. We find that, for the component of the spin susceptibility parallel to the $\mathbf{d}$ vector, a pronounced superconductivity-induced spin resonance appears at $\mathbf{Q}_{\mathrm{Y}}$ only in the $B_{2u}$ state. This behavior arises because the $B_{2u}$ order parameter remains finite and changes its sign between the relevant $f$-electron-dominated Fermi-surface regions connected by $\mathbf{Q}_\mathrm{Y}$ near $k_z=π$. The sign-change criterion is applicable to multiband superconductors in three-dimensional heavy-fermion systems, in the presence of (i) low-dimensional portions of the Fermi surface connected by a nesting vector, (ii) the dominance of the $f$-electron character, and (iii) the finite amplitude of SC gap on the portions.
summary: This work theoretically examines the magnetic excitations in the heavy-fermion superconductor UTe2 using a periodic Anderson model within the BCS-RPA formalism. It finds that the spin resonance peak, a key signature of superconductivity, appears exclusively when the superconducting order parameter belongs to the $B_{2u}$ irreducible representation. This result highlights how Fermi surface topology and pairing symmetry dictate observable magnetic responses in correlated superconductors.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamical spin response (magnetic excitations) within UTe2, a heavy-fermion superconductor suspected to exhibit spin-triplet superconductivity.
main_result: A pronounced superconductivity-induced spin resonance is found only for the $B_{2u}$ order parameter in the SC state, explained by a sign change criterion across relevant Fermi surface regions connected by $\mathbf{Q}_Y$.
method: The analysis employs the BCS-RPA formalism applied to a mixed-dimensional periodic Anderson model Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is UTe2, modeled using a three-orbital tight-binding framework (f, d, p orbitals) coupled via an on-site Coulomb interaction ($H_U$).
key_observables: Dynamical spin susceptibility ($\chi(\mathbf{q}, \omega)$), superconductivity-induced spin resonance peak, and the hybridization gap.
important_parameters: The analysis compares four odd-parity irreducible representations ($A_u, B_{1u}, B_{2u}, B_{3u}$) for the order parameter; $\mathbf{Q}_Y = (0, \pi, 0)$ is a critical nesting vector.
main_assumptions: The formalism relies on approximating the spin susceptibility using BCS-RPA and assumes applicability of the sign-change criterion derived from multiband superconductivity theory.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail; notes mention Fermi surface geometry changes based on hybridization strength ($V_{fp}$) and the location of maximum static bare spin susceptibility ($	ext{Re} \chi_0$).
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the normal state magnetic response, showing gap opening at $\mathbf{Q}_Y$. It then transitions to the SC state analysis, comparing different pairing symmetries ($A_u$ through $B_{3u}$) to pinpoint the specific symmetry ($B_{2u}$) responsible for the resonance.
why_interesting: The theoretical framework linking magnetic excitations (spin resonance) directly to the superconducting order parameter symmetry via a sign-change criterion is highly relevant for understanding unconventional pairing mechanisms in correlated electron systems.

FIG. 4. Imaginary part of the RPA spin susceptibility in the normal state plotted as a function of frequency at (a) q = QY = (0, π, 0) and (b) q = QX = (π, 0, 0). The dependence on the hybridization Vfp is shown in both panels.
